pairs.en: “And how shall I do this great evil and sin against God?” (39:9). Yosef is the aspect of rectifying judgment, the aspect of “a judgment for the God of Yaakov; He placed it as testimony in Yehosef,” etc., for Yaakov and Yosef are considered as one, and Yaakov is the aspect of judgment, as written in this verse, and as it is written, “Judgment and righteousness in Yaakov You have made.” And through this Yosef merited to stand firm in a great trial and did not blemish the covenant.

pairs.he: כִּי עִקַּר כְּבִישַׁת הַיֵּצֶר זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁפָּט, עַל יְדֵי שֶׁשּׁוֹפְטִין וְדָנִין אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי אֵינוֹ כְּדַאי לַחֲטֹא נֶגְדּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ הַגּוֹמֵל לוֹ כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת וְעָתִיד לְהִפָּרַע מִמֶּנּוּ עַל הַכֹּל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר יוֹסֵף ״אֵיךְ אֶעֱשֶׂה הָרָעָה הַגְּדֹלָה הַזֹּאת וְחָטָאתִי לֵאלֹקִים״, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה כָּבַשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ וּמָנַע אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֲבֵרָה.
pairs.en: For one merits the principal subjugation of the inclination through judgment, by judging and trying oneself oneself: certainly it is not worthwhile to sin against Him, blessed be He, who bestows all good things upon him and will exact payment from him for everything, as Yosef said, “How shall I do this great evil and sin against God?” And through this he subdued his inclination and restrained himself from the transgression.

pairs.he: כִּי זֶה עִקַּר הַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁהָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לִשְׁפֹּט אֶת עַצְמוֹ, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּשְׁפֹּט אֶת עַצְמוֹ תָּמִיד אֵיךְ רָאוּי לוֹ לְהִתְנַהֵג בְּכָל יוֹם וָיוֹם, וּבִפְרָט כְּשֶׁבָּא לִידֵי אֵיזֶה נִסָּיוֹן וּמִשְׁקָל שֶׁהַיֵּצֶר מְסִיתוֹ לְאֵיזֶה תַּאֲוָה אוֹ מִדָּה רָעָה, שֶׁאָז עִקַּר הַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִשְׁפֹּט אֶת עַצְמוֹ אִם כֵּן רָאוּי לוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת.
pairs.en: For this is the principal judgment by which a person must judge himself: that is, he must constantly judge himself as to how it is fitting for him to conduct himself each and every day, particularly when he comes to some trial and weighing, when the inclination incites him to some desire or bad trait. Then judgment is principally needed: he must judge himself whether it is thus fitting for him to act.

pairs.en: And the principal trial and weighing are in the desire for illicit relations, which is the all-encompassing evil. And there judgment is principally needed: a person must greatly fear His judgment and verdict, blessed be He, and judge himself himself and flee from the transgression, as they said: calculate the loss of a mitzvah against its reward, and the reward of a transgression against its loss. And this is as it is written, “I considered my ways and turned my feet,” etc. And this is as our master, teacher and Rabbi, of blessed memory, wrote: a person must have a settled mind, to compose himself carefully—what is the purpose of all the desires, etc. [printed note marker: 132]? All this is the aspect of the aforesaid judgment, which is principally in the aforesaid desire. And Yosef merited the aspect of complete judgment, through which he stood firm in the trial, as above.

(הלכות הרשאה הלכה ד׳ אות כ׳)
breslov.en:
“And how shall I do this great evil and sin against God?” (39:9). Yosef is the aspect of rectifying judgment, the aspect of “a judgment for the God of Yaakov; He placed it as testimony in Yehosef,” etc., for Yaakov and Yosef are considered as one, and Yaakov is the aspect of judgment, as written in this verse, and as it is written, “Judgment and righteousness in Yaakov You have made.” And through this Yosef merited to stand firm in a great trial and did not blemish the covenant.

For one merits the principal subjugation of the inclination through judgment, by judging and trying oneself oneself: certainly it is not worthwhile to sin against Him, blessed be He, who bestows all good things upon him and will exact payment from him for everything, as Yosef said, “How shall I do this great evil and sin against God?” And through this he subdued his inclination and restrained himself from the transgression.

For this is the principal judgment by which a person must judge himself: that is, he must constantly judge himself as to how it is fitting for him to conduct himself each and every day, particularly when he comes to some trial and weighing, when the inclination incites him to some desire or bad trait. Then judgment is principally needed: he must judge himself whether it is thus fitting for him to act.

And the principal trial and weighing are in the desire for illicit relations, which is the all-encompassing evil. And there judgment is principally needed: a person must greatly fear His judgment and verdict, blessed be He, and judge himself himself and flee from the transgression, as they said: calculate the loss of a mitzvah against its reward, and the reward of a transgression against its loss. And this is as it is written, “I considered my ways and turned my feet,” etc. And this is as our master, teacher and Rabbi, of blessed memory, wrote: a person must have a settled mind, to compose himself carefully—what is the purpose of all the desires, etc. [printed note marker: 132]? All this is the aspect of the aforesaid judgment, which is principally in the aforesaid desire. And Yosef merited the aspect of complete judgment, through which he stood firm in the trial, as above.

(Halachos of Authorization, Halacha 4, item 20)

זֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בְּעֵת הַנִּסָּיוֹן ׳וַתִּתְפְּשֵׂהוּ בְּבִגְדוֹ׳. ׳בְּבִגְדוֹ׳ דַּיְקָא, כִּי רָצְתָה לְהִתְאַחֵז בִּבְגָדָיו חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְלַבֵּשׁ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בִּבְגָדִים צוֹאִים. אֲבָל יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק עָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן וְלֹא רָצָה לְטַמֵּאוֹת נִשְׁמָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי בְּגָדִים צוֹאִים הַנִּמְשָׁכִין עַל יְדֵי נִאוּף. וְעַל כֵּן ׳וַיַּעֲזֹב בִּגְדוֹ בְּיָדָהּ וַיָּנָס וַיֵּצֵא הַחוּצָה׳. וְאָז דַּיְקָא בְּאוֹתָהּ הָרֶגַע הִפְשִׁיט מֵעַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת כָּל אֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים שֶׁהָיוּ נֶאֱחָזִין בִּבְגָדָיו.
pairs.en: This is what is written there at the time of the trial: ‘And she seized him by his garment.’ Specifically ‘by his garment,’ for she wanted to fasten herself onto his garments, Heaven forbid, so that he would be clothed, Heaven forbid, in filthy garments. But Yosef the righteous stood firm in the trial and did not want to defile his soul by means of filthy garments that are drawn forth through adultery. And therefore, ‘And he left his garment in her hand, and fled and went outside.’ And then, precisely at that moment, he completely stripped from himself every hold of the filthy garments that had fastened themselves onto his garments.

pairs.he: כִּי אֲפִלּוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּדוֹלִים כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ בְּנִסָּיוֹן כָּרָאוּי לָהֶם עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אֵיזֶה אֲחִיזָה מֵהַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים. וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁעָמַד יוֹסֵף בְּנִסָּיוֹן אָז דַּיְקָא הִפְשִׁיט מֵעַצְמוֹ בְּחִינַת אֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים בִּבְחִינַת ׳וַיַּעֲזֹב בִּגְדוֹ בְּיָדָהּ וַיָּנָס׳ וְכוּ׳. שֶׁהַבֶּגֶד שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ אֲחִיזָה בּוֹ עָזַב בְּיָדָהּ. וְהִפְשִׁיט אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִבְּגָדִים אֵלּוּ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת.
pairs.en: For even the great righteous people, so long as they have not stood firm in a trial as befits them, still have in them some hold of the filthy garments. And therefore, when Yosef stood firm in the trial, then precisely he stripped from himself the aspect of the hold of the filthy garments, in the aspect of ‘And he left his garment in her hand and fled,’ etc.: the garment in which she had a hold he left in her hand, and he completely stripped himself of these garments.

pairs.he: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ יוֹסֵף מִדִּלֵּהּ נָטַל וְכוּ׳. וּמִגֹּדֶל עֹצֶם צִדְקָתוֹ שֶׁעָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן בָּזֶה זָכָה לְהַמְשִׁיךְ בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים לְכָל אֶחָיו בִּבְחִינַת ׳לְכֻלָּם נָתַן לָאִישׁ חֲלִפוֹת שְׂמָלֹת׳ וְכוּ׳. שֶׁמֵּרֹב שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ לְתַקֵּן כֻּלָּם לְהַמְשִׁיךְ לָהֶם בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים. וְעַל כֵּן וּלְבִנְיָמִין נָתַן וְכוּ׳ וְחָמֵשׁ חֲלִפֹת שְׂמָלֹת, שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁהָיָה מַחֲלִיף בְּגָדָיו חֲמִשָּׁה פְּעָמִים בְּיוֹם כִּפּוּר כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בָּנוּי בְּחֶלְקוֹ כַּמּוּבָא. כִּי עִקַּר בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים בְּגָדִים לְבָנִים זָכָה הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל. שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה מְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
pairs.en: And [this is] as is stated in the holy Zohar, “Yosef took from his own,” etc. And through the greatness of the immensity of his righteousness—in that he stood firm in the trial— through this he merited to draw forth the aspect of clean garments for all his brothers, in the aspect of ‘To all of them he gave each man changes of clothing,’ etc.—for he had so much power to rectify them all, to draw forth for them the aspect of clean garments. And therefore, [it is stated:] “and to Binyamin he gave,” etc., “and five changes of clothing,” which alludes to the garments of the High Priest, who changed his garments five times on Yom Kippur when he entered the Temple, which was built in [Binyamin’s] portion, as is cited. For the High Priest merited the principal aspect of clean garments, white garments; for through this he would atone for all Israel.

זֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בְּעֵת הַנִּסָּיוֹן ׳וַתִּתְפְּשֵׂהוּ בְּבִגְדוֹ׳. ׳בְּבִגְדוֹ׳ דַּיְקָא, כִּי רָצְתָה לְהִתְאַחֵז בִּבְגָדָיו חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְלַבֵּשׁ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בִּבְגָדִים צוֹאִים. אֲבָל יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק עָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן וְלֹא רָצָה לְטַמֵּאוֹת נִשְׁמָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי בְּגָדִים צוֹאִים הַנִּמְשָׁכִין עַל יְדֵי נִאוּף. וְעַל כֵּן ׳וַיַּעֲזֹב בִּגְדוֹ בְּיָדָהּ וַיָּנָס וַיֵּצֵא הַחוּצָה׳. וְאָז דַּיְקָא בְּאוֹתָהּ הָרֶגַע הִפְשִׁיט מֵעַצְמוֹ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת כָּל אֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים שֶׁהָיוּ נֶאֱחָזִין בִּבְגָדָיו.

כִּי אֲפִלּוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים הַגְּדוֹלִים כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ בְּנִסָּיוֹן כָּרָאוּי לָהֶם עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אֵיזֶה אֲחִיזָה מֵהַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים. וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁעָמַד יוֹסֵף בְּנִסָּיוֹן אָז דַּיְקָא הִפְשִׁיט מֵעַצְמוֹ בְּחִינַת אֲחִיזַת הַבְּגָדִים הַצּוֹאִים בִּבְחִינַת ׳וַיַּעֲזֹב בִּגְדוֹ בְּיָדָהּ וַיָּנָס׳ וְכוּ׳. שֶׁהַבֶּגֶד שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ אֲחִיזָה בּוֹ עָזַב בְּיָדָהּ. וְהִפְשִׁיט אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִבְּגָדִים אֵלּוּ בִּשְׁלֵמוּת.

וְאָז זָכָה אַחַר כָּךְ לִבְגָדִים נְקִיִּים וִיקָרִים בִּבְחִינַת ׳וַיַּלְבֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ בִּגְדֵי שֵׁשׁ׳ וְכוּ׳.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ יוֹסֵף מִדִּלֵּהּ נָטַל וְכוּ׳. וּמִגֹּדֶל עֹצֶם צִדְקָתוֹ שֶׁעָמַד בְּנִסָּיוֹן בָּזֶה זָכָה לְהַמְשִׁיךְ בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים לְכָל אֶחָיו בִּבְחִינַת ׳לְכֻלָּם נָתַן לָאִישׁ חֲלִפוֹת שְׂמָלֹת׳ וְכוּ׳. שֶׁמֵּרֹב שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ כֹּחַ לְתַקֵּן כֻּלָּם לְהַמְשִׁיךְ לָהֶם בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים. וְעַל כֵּן וּלְבִנְיָמִין נָתַן וְכוּ׳ וְחָמֵשׁ חֲלִפֹת שְׂמָלֹת, שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז עַל בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁהָיָה מַחֲלִיף בְּגָדָיו חֲמִשָּׁה פְּעָמִים בְּיוֹם כִּפּוּר כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בָּנוּי בְּחֶלְקוֹ כַּמּוּבָא. כִּי עִקַּר בְּחִינַת בְּגָדִים נְקִיִּים בְּגָדִים לְבָנִים זָכָה הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל. שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הָיָה מְכַפֵּר עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל.

breslov.en:
Yosef completely stripped from himself the hold of the filthy garments.

“And she seized him by his garment, etc.; and he left his garment in her hand, and fled and went outside.”

(39:12)

This is what is written there at the time of the trial: ‘And she seized him by his garment.’ Specifically ‘by his garment,’ for she wanted to fasten herself onto his garments, Heaven forbid, so that he would be clothed, Heaven forbid, in filthy garments. But Yosef the righteous stood firm in the trial and did not want to defile his soul by means of filthy garments that are drawn forth through adultery. And therefore, ‘And he left his garment in her hand, and fled and went outside.’ And then, precisely at that moment, he completely stripped from himself every hold of the filthy garments that had fastened themselves onto his garments.

For even the great righteous people, so long as they have not stood firm in a trial as befits them, still have in them some hold of the filthy garments. And therefore, when Yosef stood firm in the trial, then precisely he stripped from himself the aspect of the hold of the filthy garments, in the aspect of ‘And he left his garment in her hand and fled,’ etc.: the garment in which she had a hold he left in her hand, and he completely stripped himself of these garments.

And then he afterward merited clean and precious garments, in the aspect of ‘And he clothed him in garments of fine linen,’ etc.

And [this is] as is stated in the holy Zohar, “Yosef took from his own,” etc. And through the greatness of the immensity of his righteousness—in that he stood firm in the trial— through this he merited to draw forth the aspect of clean garments for all his brothers, in the aspect of ‘To all of them he gave each man changes of clothing,’ etc.—for he had so much power to rectify them all, to draw forth for them the aspect of clean garments. And therefore, [it is stated:] “and to Binyamin he gave,” etc., “and five changes of clothing,” which alludes to the garments of the High Priest, who changed his garments five times on Yom Kippur when he entered the Temple, which was built in [Binyamin’s] portion, as is cited. For the High Priest merited the principal aspect of clean garments, white garments; for through this he would atone for all Israel.

(Halachos of סעודה [The Meal], halacha 5, item 20)

pairs.en: Most desire for money is on account of clothes and garments, as everyone can understand for himself: most of the toil and preoccupation of earning a livelihood is on account of the clothes and garments of honor for himself and his wife and his sons and his daughters, and especially at the time of marriage, when he must marry them off, when all the abundance of expenditure is on garments. pairs.he: הגה״ק רבי הירש מיכל שפירא ז״ל בצבי לצדיק (מכתב ג׳) כתב: בהיות כי עם ה׳ נפרדו לחברות ומפלגות שונות אמת כי כולם קדושים, וכולם חפצים לעבוד את ה׳ ולהבין עמקי תורתינו הקדושה וסדר העבודה הטהורה הנכונה. וכל חברה וחברה מעמיק בטהור לבבם למצוא לעצמם ולאחרים דרך ומסלול לאחוז בלב שלם באבינו שבשמים. אבל לסיבות אריכות הגלות וההסתר פנים בעוה״ר, מצא היצר פתח בזה עצמו, לגרום התרחקות בין אדם לחבירו בכל אופן שישנו במציאות. ומי שאינו טורח ביגיעה רבה בפרט זה, נדמה לו שכל הטורח של חבירו למען לקרב עצמו לאבינו שבשמים, הוא ח״ו ההיפך מזה - התרחקות מאתו יתברך. ע״כ. והנצי״ב מוולוז׳ין ז״ל כתב (הקדמת ספרו העמק דבר על התורה): בית שני היה דור עיקש ופתלתול. ופירשנו שהיו צדיקים וחסידים ועמלי תורה, אך לא היו ישרים בהליכות עולמים. על כן מפני שנאת חינם שבלבם זה את זה, חשדו את מי שראו שנוהג שלא כדעתם ביראת ה׳, שהוא צדוקי ואפיקורס. ובאו עי"ז לידי ש"ד בדרך הפלגה ולכל הרעות שבעולם עד שחרב הבית. ועל זה היה צידוק הדין, שהקב״ה ישר הוא ואינו סובל צדיקים כאלו. אלא באופן שהולכים בדרך הישר גם בהליכות עולם, ולא בעקמימות אע״ג שהוא לשם שמים. ע״כ.
pairs.en: The holy gaon Rabbi Hirsch Michel Shapira, of blessed memory, wrote in Tzvi LaTzaddik (letter 3): Since the people of the Lord have separated into various societies and factions, it is true that they are all holy, and they all wish to serve the Lord and to understand the depths of our holy Torah and the order of the proper, pure service. And each and every society delves, in the purity of their hearts, to find for themselves and for others a way and a path to hold fast wholeheartedly to our Father in Heaven. But, owing to the prolongation of exile and the concealment of the face, on account of our many sins, the inclination found an opening in this very thing, to cause distance between one person and his fellow in every manner that exists in reality. And one who does not labor with great exertion in this particular matter imagines that all his fellow’s toil to draw himself near to our Father in Heaven is, Heaven forbid, the opposite of this—distance from Him, blessed be He. End of quotation. And the Netziv of Volozhin, of blessed memory, wrote (the introduction to his book Haamek Davar on the Torah): The Second Temple period was a crooked and perverse generation. And we have explained that they were righteous and pious and toilers in Torah, but they were not upright in their worldly conduct. Therefore, because of baseless hatred in their hearts toward one another, they suspected anyone whom they saw conducting himself not according to their view in fear of the Lord of being a Sadducee and a heretic. pairs.he: ובהלכות נזקי שכנים (הלכה ה׳ אות ב׳) כתב מוהרנ״ת ז״ל: כל אחד מישראל כפי שרשו משבטו שמשם נוסח וסדר תפלתו וכפי מעשיו כן האמת שלו. ומזה נמשכים ריבוי השינויים שבין אחד לחבירו אפילו הכשרים והישרים. כי זה מתפלל בארוכה וזה במהירות זה בקול רם וזה בקול נמוך וכיוצא בזה שינויים לאין מספר אע״פ ששניהם כוונתם רצויה באמת, כי אע״פ ששניהם כוונתם באמת אעפ״כ האמת של כל אחד משונה מחבירו, ועל כן אסור לאדם להסתכל בחבירו לרעה אע״פ שנדמה לו לפי האמת שלו שחבירו אינו מתנהג באמת ואינו מתפלל באמת, כי מי יודע האמת של חבירו. כי לפי דעתו יכול לטעות שאין בחבירו אמת מחמת שאינו מתנהג כפי דעתו, אבל באמת גם חבירו כוונתו אל האמת לפי מדרגתו ושרשו. ע״כ.

For who knows the truth of his fellow? For according to his own understanding he may mistakenly think that there is no truth in his fellow because he does not conduct himself according to his understanding; but in truth his fellow too directs his intention toward the truth according to his level and his root. כתב הרמח״ל (אוצרות רמח״ל) פרשת שמיני וז״ל: אמרו חז״ל כשם שהעוף אינו פורח אלא בכנפיו כך ישראל אינם יכולים לעשות שום דבר בלתי חוקים. והסוד הוא, ישראל עושים תיקונים. אבל אולי לא יעלו ויפרחו למקומם שהס״א תעכב. לזה צריך כח החוקים שממש עושים פעולת העוף הפורח בכנפיו, ובכח התקנה שלהם מעמידים אורות אלו להציל התיקונים מיד הס״א ולהעלותם למקומם. ע״כ.
pairs.en: The Ramchal wrote (Otzros HaRamchal), parsha Shemini, and these are his words: Our Sages, of blessed memory, said: Just as a bird does not fly except with its wings, so Israel cannot do anything without statutes. And the secret is this: Israel perform rectifications. But perhaps they will not rise and fly to their place, for the sitra achra would obstruct. For this the power of the statutes is needed, which actually perform the action of a bird flying with its wings; and by the power of their enactment they set up these lights to save the rectifications from the hand of the sitra achra and to raise them to their place. Thus far.

pairs.he: ועוד כתב הרמח״ל בפרשת פקודי שם: התיקונים הראשיים הם צריכים להעשות על ידי היותר חשובים שבישראל, והם מתקנים בשביל כל ישראל. ולכן בצלאל עשה המשכן שהיה משבט יהודה, החשוב שבשבטים והוא תיקן בשביל כולם. ע״כ. וכתב הרמח״ל בתיקונים חדשים (תיקון ז׳): וכל חכם לב בכם יבואו ויעשו, לאתקנא בגין כלא, ואית דאיהו לחודיה יכיל לאתקנא בגין כל ישראל, כד״א ויקם משה את המשכן, דהא כל אלין עברין אתעבידו בתיקונא דכל חד בדיליה, אבל כלא לא אשתלים ולא אתתקן אלא ע״י דמשה דאיהו שקיל ככל ישראל. מצדיקי הרבים אלין חכמי לב דאתמר דמתקני תיקוניה לכלהו ישראל, אבל המשכילים אלין משה ותרין משיחין דקיימין לאשתא על כלהו אחרנין, בגין ויביאו את המשכן אל משה, דהא איהו נטיל תדיר כל תיקונא דכלהו לאשלמא מילין כדקא יאות.
pairs.en: And the Ramchal further wrote there in the parsha Pekuday: The principal rectifications must be performed by the most distinguished among Israel, and they rectify on behalf of all Israel. And therefore Betzalel made the Tabernacle, for he was from the tribe of Yehudah, the most distinguished of the tribes, and he rectified on behalf of all of them. Thus far. For this the power of the statutes is needed, which actually perform the action of a bird flying with its wings; and by the power of their enactment they set up these lights to save the rectifications from the hand of the sitra achra and to raise them to their place. במגלה עמוקות (על ואתחנן אופן רנ״ב): זה ענין מכירת יוסף שראו השבטים שעתיד ירבעם לעמוד ממנו שהוא יהיה בסוד מרכבה טמאה, שהיא ׳כלב רע׳ ושמו של ירבעם מוכיח עליו שכן ירבעם עולה בחושבן ׳מרכבה טמאה׳ ׳כלב רע׳ ולכן אמרו ז״ל במדרש על פסוק ׳והנה בעל החלומות׳ שאמרו זה עתיד להשיאנו לבעלים ועתה נהרוג את הכלבים מדה כנגד מדה. וז״ש הפסוק וראו אותו מרחוק ויתנכלו אותו להמיתו, ר״ל שראו מה שלעתיד יצא מאתו, שירבעם יצא ממנו, ועתה לכו ונהרגהו, ר״ל עכשיו נהרגהו קודם שיצא ממנו. ע״כ.
pairs.en: In Megaleh Amukos (on Vaeschanan, exposition 252): This is the matter of the sale of Yosef: the tribes saw that Yeravam was destined to arise from him, who would be in the mystery of an impure chariot, which is an ‘evil dog’; and Yeravam’s name demonstrates this concerning him, for Yeravam amounts, in numerical reckoning, to ‘impure chariot,’ ‘evil dog.’ And therefore our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash on the verse ‘And behold, the master of dreams’ that they said: This one is destined to lead us astray to the baals, and now let us kill the dogs, measure for measure. And this is what the verse says: “And they saw him from afar, and they conspired against him to put him to death,” meaning that they saw what would come forth from him in the future, that Yeravam would come forth from him; “and now, let us go and kill him,” meaning: Now let us kill him before he comes forth from him. Thus far.

pairs.he: קלב.

בליקוטי מוהר״ן (חלק שני סימן י׳): מה שהעולם רחוקים מהשם יתברך ואינם מתקרבים אליו יתברך, הוא רק מחמת שאין להם ישוב הדעת, ואינם מישבין עצמם. והעקר להשתדל לישב עצמו היטב. מה התכלית מכל התאוות ומכל עניני העולם הזה, הן תאוות הנכנסות לגוף, הן תאוות שחוץ לגוף, כגון כבוד, ואז בודאי ישוב אל ה׳. ע״כ.
pairs.en: In Likutay Moharan (Part Two, section 10): That people are far from Hashem, blessed be He, and do not draw near to Him, blessed be He, is only because they do not have settled understanding, and they do not settle their minds. And the essential thing is to endeavor to settle one’s mind thoroughly. What is the ultimate purpose of all the desires and of all the affairs of this world, both desires that enter the body and desires outside the body, such as honor? And then one will certainly return to Hashem. Thus far.
